'''Stephen Andrew Bustin''' (born 1954)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Stephen_Bustin2/info/|title=Stephen Bustin|work=[[ResearchGate]]|access-date=24 September 2013}}</ref> is a British scientist, former professor of molecular sciences at [[Queen Mary University of London]] from 2004 to 2012, as well as visiting professor at [[Middlesex University]], beginning in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://selectbiosciences.com/conferences/biographies.aspx?speaker=25335&conf=QPCRA2012|title=Stephen Bustin's Biography|publisher=Selectbiosciences|date=2011|access-date=12 August 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dddmag.com/articles/2007/10/how-reliable-your-qpcr-data|title=How Reliable is Your qPCR Data?|work=Drug Discovery & Development|date=10 May 2007|access-date=12 December 2013|author=McGee, Patrick}}</ref> In 2012 he was appointed Professor of Allied Health and Medicine at [[Anglia Ruskin University]].<ref name=QPCR>{{cite web|url=http://www.qpcrexpert.com/|title=Definitive qPCR|date=2013|access-date=12 August 2013|author=Bustin, Stephen}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=January 2026|reason=This is just some Wordpress site with no specific information about Bustin.}} He is known{{By whom|date=December 2025}} for his research into [[polymerase chain reaction]].

==Education==
Bustin obtained his B.A. and PhD from [[Trinity College, Dublin]] in molecular genetics.<ref name=anglia>{{cite web|url=http://www.anglia.ac.uk/medical-science/about/our-staff/stephen-bustin|title=Stephen Bustin|work=Anglia Ruskin University|access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref>{{Dead link|date=December 2025}}

==Career==
In 2023, Bustin was elected a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stephen Bustin|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Bustin_Stephen|work=Member|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2024-11-02}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2026}}

==Research==
His research group's general areas of interest are the small and large bowel, as well as [[colorectal cancer]] with particular emphasis on investigating the process of invasion and metastasis. An important aim is to translate molecular techniques into clinical practice by including molecular parameters into clinical tumor staging.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://webinar.sciencemag.org/webinar/archive/future-qpcr|title=The future of qPCR|publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|date=30 September 2010|access-date=11 August 2013}}</ref> To this end, Bustin has published many papers on PCR techniques,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nolan|first1=T.|last2=Hands|first2=R. E.|last3=Bustin|first3=S. A.|doi=10.1038/nprot.2006.236|title=Quantification of mRNA using real-time RT-PCR|journal=Nature Protocols|volume=1|issue=3|pages=1559–1582|year=2006|pmid=17406449|s2cid=10108148}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mueller|first1=R.|last2=Bustin|first2=S. A.|doi=10.1042/CS20050086|title=Real-time reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) and its potential use in clinical diagnosis|journal=Clinical Science|volume=109|issue=4|pages=365–379|year=2005|pmid=16171460}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=January 2026|reason=To include this, we actually need a source that states that Bustn has published "many papers", not just link to two of them.}} in particular [[reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction]], the subject of his most cited paper, published in 2000.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bustin|first1=S.|title=Absolute quantification of mRNA using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction assays|doi=10.1677/jme.0.0250169|journal=Journal of Molecular Endocrinology|volume=25|issue=2|pages=169–193|year=2000|pmid=11013345|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Bustin led a group who the [[MIQE guidelines]] in a 2009 paper published in ''[[Clinical Chemistry (journal)|Clinical Chemistry]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bustin|first1=S. A.|last2=Benes|first2=V.|last3=Garson|first3=J. A.|last4=Hellemans|first4=J.|last5=Huggett|first5=J.|last6=Kubista|first6=M.|last7=Mueller|first7=R.|last8=Nolan|first8=T.|last9=Pfaffl|first9=M. W.|last10=Shipley|first10=G. L.|last11=Vandesompele|first11=J.|last12=Wittwer|first12=C. T.|doi=10.1373/clinchem.2008.112797|title=The MIQE Guidelines: Minimum Information for Publication of Quantitative Real-Time PCR Experiments|journal=Clinical Chemistry|volume=55|issue=4|pages=611–622|year=2009|pmid=19246619|doi-access=free}}</ref> the goal of which is to create guidelines for how PCR should be performed to ensure that PCR results are being reliably conducted and interpreted, as well as to make replication of experiments easier.
This paper is the fifth most cited one ever to be published in ''Clinical Chemistry'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.miqe.info/|title=The MIQE Guidelines|access-date=11 August 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clinchem.org/reports/most-cited|title=Most Cited Articles|work=[[Clinical Chemistry (journal)|Clinical Chemistry]]|access-date=9 September 2013}}</ref> with over 17000 citations on [[Google Scholar]] as of September 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=F62lTaUAAAAJ&citation_for_view=F62lTaUAAAAJ:d1gkVwhDpl0C|title = The MIQE Guidelines: M inimum I nformation for Publication of Q uantitative Real-Time PCR e xperiments}}</ref>

==Lundy murders testimony==
Bustin testified in the trials pertaining to the [[Lundy murders]] in 2015, criticizing tests that had claimed to detect human brain cells on Mark Lundy's shirt.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11415544|title=Mark Lundy retrial: DNA on shirt matched to victim|work=[[New Zealand Herald]]|date=11 March 2015|access-date=30 August 2015|author=Quilliam, Rebecca}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/crime/67123673/Mark-Lundy-murder-retrial-Day-20|title=Mark Lundy murder retrial: Day 20|work=[[Stuff.co.nz]]|date=9 March 2015|access-date=30 August 2015|author=Galuszka, Jono}}</ref>
